parts.label: (b)
(b)(i)
parts.text:
The current in the circuit is $1.1 \times 10^{-2}\ \text{A}$. The potential difference across $Y$ is $4.0\ \text{V}$.

Calculate the resistance of $X$.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
The temperature of $Y$ is changed to $190^{\circ}\text{C}$. The resistance of $X$ remains unchanged.

Determine the new potential difference across $Y$.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
The resistance of $X$ is increased. The temperature of $Y$ remains at $190^{\circ}\text{C}$.

By reference to the current in the circuit, state and explain the effect of this change, if any, on the potential difference **across $Y$**.
